messages.author: 7f4d6a4e00c83b7e
messages.subject: Enough data for AKDE estimation
parts:
Dear Christen,

I hope you're doing well. I'm currently working on calculating the home range using the AKDE function, but I have some questions regarding my dataset.

I’m using VHF collars, and my minimum sampling interval is more than 24 hours, range 48 or 72 hours. I’m encountering some issues while fitting the models, and I’m unsure whether my data are suitable for AKDE rather than traditional KDE. The period I’m working with spans 3 months, and I have a total of 20–25 locations.

  1. Can I apply AKDE with this type of data? My variogram looks like the attached image.
  2. When I proceed with the script, I do get an AKDE representation, assuming Brownian Motion (BM) as the best model,  because the ctmm.fit doesnt works for me in order to get an AIC value  . However, I'm concerned about whether this is appropriate given the small number of locations and the long intervals between them. 

Could you please provide some guidance on whether AKDE is a valid approach here?

Thank you in advance for your time,

Mariola

messages.author: 7d868ffe3daa8319
messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] Enough data for AKDE estimation
parts:
Hi Mariola,

This animal does not look range-resident to me--the variogram does not ever asymptote. In this case, neither AKDE nor KDE would be an appropriate model because this animal does not have a home range.

Jesse

messages.author: 7d868ffe3daa8319
messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] Enough data for AKDE estimation
parts:
Hi Mariola,

The data presented suggests that this individual is not resident, at least for the entire duration of the time period used here. But it may be that the migration pathway or part of it has not totally been cut out of the movement track--it is totally possible that the animal was resident within part (or even most) of the movement track displayed.

Brownian motion is not suitable for range distribution estimation because it is not a range-resident model. There is more information in the Concepts and Definitions section here: https://doi.org/10.1101/2022.09.29.509951

Jesse

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] Enough data for AKDE estimation
parts:
Hi Mariola,

I would compare the empirical variogram that you have plotted to the theoretical variogram of the selected range resident model, which I assume is OU or IID. If Jesse is correct, there will be a large discrepancy between them where their CIs do not overlap.

I would also plot the locations colored by time to check for an obvious range shift or migration.

Best,
Chris
